notes: Perfect claim overlap (C23-C29, C98) on journey/task-demand remapping findings. LLM found ANCOVA controls sufficient for behavioral confounds, while peer reviewers expressed major concerns that confounds (location, speed, head direction) were inadequately controlled, stating 'the ANCOVAs are not detecting this confound' and requesting spatial restriction analyses.

High overlap (90.9%) on background literature claims about hippocampal function, place cells, episodic memory, and remapping. Both agree these foundational concepts are well-established and properly cited.

Strong overlap (71.4%) on hierarchical organization and generalization claims (C30-C31, C87, C90-C91). LLM found cross-subtask generalization analysis robust, while peer reviewers found the analysis 'difficult to follow' with Figure 7 'hard to interpret,' requesting additional comparative analyses before accepting pattern completion claims.

Good overlap (72.7%) on main findings about simultaneous representation of spatiotemporal and non-spatial contexts (C4-C5, C35, C41-C43, C92-C93). LLM found converging evidence sufficient, while peer reviewers expressed uncertainty pending resolution of behavioral confound concerns that 'could undermine the conclusions.'

Strong overlap (66.7%) on episode classification and prospective coding claims (C32-C34, C103). LLM found binary classification with statistical testing convincing, while peer reviewers requested comparative analysis of 'relative ability to classify into trajectories vs tasks vs specific trial types,' suggesting insufficient evidence for claims about equal coding strength.

Moderate overlap (38.9%) on experimental design and methodology claims (C17-C19, C47-C57). Both agree the basic methods, sample sizes, recording equipment, and behavioral training protocols are appropriate and well-documented.

Exact overlap (50%) on computational/statistical methods (C74-C81). LLM found ANCOVA and trajectory analysis methods appropriate, while peer reviewers expressed concern that 'the ANCOVAs are not detecting this confound,' suggesting the implementation rather than the method itself needs refinement.

Moderate overlap (36.1%) on behavioral task design and controls (C58-C68, C106, C110-C112). Both agree the task design with MFB stimulation, lighting controls, and high performance metrics is well-controlled and appropriate.

Exact overlap (50%) on broader functional interpretations (C44, C95-C96). Both agree these claims about dual hippocampal roles in navigation and episodic memory are inferential and depend on validity of empirical findings, which remain under question.

Partial overlap (21.4%) on functional role claims (C6, C45-C46). Both agree these theoretical interpretations about dual hippocampal function are largely inferential and not directly tested through causal manipulations.
Small overlap (9.1%) on knowledge gap identification (C3, C40). Both agree the study addresses an important gap in understanding how different types of hippocampal coding relate to each other.

Small overlap (12.5%) on behavioral timing inference (C84-C85). Both express uncertainty about inferring exact cue detection and decision timing from indirect behavioral measures, which affects interpretation of temporal neural dynamics.

Minimal overlap (18.2%) on trajectory analysis claims (C88-C89). LLM found evidence for hierarchical organization supported, while peer reviewers' concerns about behavioral confounds extend to these trajectory-based claims.

Minimal overlap (2.5%) on behavioral timing (C63). LLM expressed uncertainty about indirect timing measures, while peer reviewers did not challenge the basic behavioral methodology, focusing instead on spatial analysis concerns.
Small overlap (6.8%) on spike sorting and cell classification methods (C69-C70, C72). Both implicitly accept these standard preprocessing methods as appropriate.

No direct pairing in suggested list. Peer R8 addresses place field properties and trajectory shifts (C22, C99-C102) subject to behavioral confound concerns, while LLM R8 addresses behavioral timing inference (C63, C82-C85). Both express uncertainty but on different aspects.
